review_candidates.description: CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats. CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com. Role Overview We are seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical Systems Engineer with landing gear expertise to own the landing gear system for a Massed Modular Aircraft (MMA) program, supporting a platform architecture designed for low-cost, high-rate, distributed production. This role owns the landing gear, wheels, tires, brakes, steering, and retraction/extension system from concept through qualification and production transition, including adaptation of flight-proven donor gear for the prototype and development of a bespoke, mass-producible gear for production, with particular emphasis on modularity, producibility, and design-for-manufacture principles that enable rapid, scalable build rates across multiple production sites or partners. The ideal candidate brings deep landing gear design and integration expertise combined with a strong producibility/manufacturing mindset suited to attritable, low-cost, or distributed-production aircraft concepts, rather than traditional low-rate, highly customized airframe programs. Responsibilities Own the landing gear system from requirements definition through donor gear adaptation, substantiation, first flight, and production gear development, with loads and backup structure coordinated by interface control agreements with the Structures group. Lead the donor gear survey and selection, acquire and inspect units, and execute the adaptation engineering, including attachment fittings, kinematics, retraction and extension, steering, braking and anti-skid, and weight-on-wheels and position sensing. Lead gear architecture trades (fixed versus retractable, electromechanical versus hydromechanical actuation, stowage packaging against mass, volume, and ground handling needs), converge gear geometry (tip-over, load points, and stroke) with the frozen outer mold line, close drop and energy sizing, and run the full-travel kinematics clash sweep in the digital mock-up ahead of PDR. Own the gear installation design lifecycle: linkage kinematics, clearance envelopes, load paths, material selection, tolerance stack-ups, and drawing release, and size and select wheels, tires, brakes, shock absorption, actuators, and nose-wheel steering for the landing and taxi envelopes. Substantiate the installed donor gear configuration by read-across and delta analysis against the donor aircraft basis, with drop test where read-across gaps demand it, and deliver gear reactions and substantiation evidence to Structures and to Test, Safety, and Airworthiness. Define the interface control document and performance specification for the production gear, apply DFM/DFA and common-interface principles so the gear can be produced and installed at rate across sites, support vendor selection and contract commitment, and lead that development toward the production readiness review. Capture measured ground and flight loads, taxi and landing dynamics, and donor gear lessons during flight test as the requirements basis for the production gear. Lead load analysis (gear ground loads, braking loads, steering loads), kinematic analysis, and reliability/durability analysis for the landing gear system. Perform system safety analysis (FHA, FMEA, fault tree, and zonal analysis) for the landing gear system in accordance with the program airworthiness basis. Coordinate and provide technical direction to third-party engineering services supporting the discipline, including scope definition, work package assignment, review and acceptance of deliverables, and integration of their output into the program design, analysis, and configuration baselines. Own and coordinate execution of the landing gear test program, including test fixture design, retraction rig testing, brake and steering functional testing, drop test as required, aircraft ground test, taxi test, and flight test support, and conduct root cause investigations for landing gear anomalies. Manage landing gear, wheel, brake, tire, and steering vendors, including specifications, acceptance data, qualification and acceptance test witnessing, and delivery tracking against build need for each ship-set. Prepare and present design review packages at PDR, CDR, and test readiness reviews, and maintain qualification documentation supporting airworthiness substantiation against applicable military and civil-derivative standards (MIL-STD/MIL-HDBK guidance, SAE ARPs). Minimum Requirements Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related discipline. 8+ years of aircraft mechanical systems experience with a primary focus on landing gear systems that have been built, tested, and flown. Strong background in landing gear design, including shock strut sizing and oleo-pneumatic performance, kinematics, structural attachments, wheels and brakes, tires, steering, and retraction and extension systems. Experience with ground loads and landing dynamics, including drop test planning and correlation and taxi, braking, and turning load cases. Strong systems engineering skills, including requirements management, interface definition, and system safety assessment per ARP4754A/ARP4761 or MIL-STD-882. Experience authoring specifications and statements of work and managing landing gear or wheel and brake vendors through qualification and acceptance. Proficiency in 3D CAD and PLM (NX, CATIA, or Creo), GD&T and tolerance stack-ups, classical stress and fatigue hand calculations backed by FEA, and dynamics/simulation tools (Adams, Simulink, or equivalent). Preferred Requirements Direct experience with modular, attritable, low-cost, or mass-producible aircraft/unmanned aircraft system (UAS) programs. Experience adapting donor landing gear or other flight-proven equipment to a new or prototype aircraft. Experience with electric brakes, brake-by-wire, and integration of gear, brake, and steering control with an autonomous flight control system, and familiarity with SAE ARP1311, AIR1489, ARP5265, AS6053, MIL-A-8866/8867, and JSSG-2009. Experience with UAV, autonomous, or rotorcraft landing systems or arresting gear, and machine-shop or fabrication experience. Ability to obtain/maintain Secret/Top Secret/SCI clearance. Why CHAOS? Health Benefits: medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more Our Perks: rree daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code Compensation Components: competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices Salary Range: $180,000 - $230,000 The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.
